title: Machine learning links cell response states to nanoparticle biosafety in neural systems
summary: A response-centred machine learning framework built on 893 contexts from 599 neurological studies raised ROC-AUC for biosafety from 0.66 to 0.88 and for recovery from 0.64 to 0.77 when exposure and biological context were added to material properties; adding cellular-response programmes gave 0.90 and 0.78. The model was evaluated in unseen nanocomposites using 2D and 3D microglial models and independent transcriptomic datasets. The training data are literature-derived and heterogeneous; this is a version 1 preprint abstract.
ai_technology: Response-centred machine learning framework defining a Conserved Response Axis from heterogeneous biological responses
organization: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: Experimental evaluation on unseen nanocomposites in 2D and 3D microglial models plus independent brain, lung and liver transcriptomic datasets.
evidence.unknown: Which exposures generalize beyond the compiled studies and in vivo relevance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Learns an organizing axis of response states that predicts biosafety and recovery outcomes.
